full_judgment:
Muhammad Imman Ali J. This petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 05.12.2011 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.23523 of 2009 making the Rule absolute. 

 2. The relevant facts of the case are as follows: 

 5. On 15.01.2009 the case record of Shahbagh Police Station Case No. 22(10)08 was placed before the learned Judge of the Metropolitan Special Tribunal No.1, Dhaka. The date of cognizance hearing was fixed on 26.2.2009 and cognizance taken under section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 (Act II of 1947), and warrant of arrest was issued against the accused-petitioner since he was absconding. 

 6. On the next date the accused remained absconding and on 17.05.2009 he was shown arrested and an application for bail made on behalf of accused respondent No.1 but the same was rejected. The case was transferred to the Court of Special Judge, Court No.2, Dhaka where date was fixed on 22.06.2009 for charge hearing. On the next two dates the accused sought adjournment. When another date was fixed for 26.07.2009, the accused filed an application under section 241A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. The next date fixed was 17.08.2009 for charge hearing. 

 7. On 9.8.2009 the accused respondent No.1 filed Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 23523 of 2009 before the High Court Division under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure and obtained Rule and prayed for quashing the proceedings of Metro Special Case No. 53 of 2009 pending in the Court of Special Judge, Court No.2, Dhaka. 

 8. By the impugned judgment and order, the High Court Division made the Rule absolute thereby quashed the proceedings of Special Case No.14 of 2009. 

 9. Mr. Murad Reza, the learned Additional Attorney General appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that the High Court Division failed to appreciate that there is a prima facie case against the accused respondent No. 1 who as the General Secretary of the B.M.A. by abusing his power gained benefit for B.M.A. and at the same time caused loss of Tk. 20,43,250/- to the Dhaka Shishu Hospital. He further submits that the accused returned 3,71,500 tickets showing them as unsold after the draw of the lottery had taken place on 28.02.2004 while back dating the return of those tickets to 23.02.2004. Thus he committed an offence under section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 (II of 1947). 

 "I. For that the High Court Division while making the me absolute in connection with the instant case under section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 (II of 1947) now pending before the Court of Special Judge, Court No. 2, Dhaka, failed to appreciate there is a strong prima-facie case and specific overt act against the accused respondent that while he was general secretary of B.M.A. at that time with a view to make B.M.A. benefited, caused loss of Tk. 20,43,250/- to Dhaka Shishu Hospital by purchasing lottery tickets on credit and thereafter by way of returning the said tickets without payment, after draw of the lottery took place, by showing the same as unsold; and
